sourceRefs.locator: Hull and rowing holes, the ship built in 820, burial of two women in 834 and the uncertainty over their identities and status.
Opening account of the burial and the four sleighs, followed by “Carvings and ornamentation”. The museum distinguishes three richly carved sleighs and discusses their use before burial.
Opening paragraphs on the Chronicle and the Irish annals, Old Norse víking/víkingr and the raiding voyages underlying one sense of the term.
